ll. I have perused the materials on record and considered the rival arguments. It appears to me that the workman 
did not perform his duty seriously and sincerely. It is an admitted fact that he remained absent for more than five 
months without any authorization. The workman failed to produce any medical papers in support of his plea of illness. 
In the affidavit-in-chief the workman stated that after recovery from illness he reported for duty but was not allowed 
to join. He did not mention any date when he reported for duty. The workman was fully aware about issuance of 
Charge Sheet and in paragraph no. (5) of the affidavit-in-chief he stated that when Charge Sheet was issued, he was 
in the Colliery and the Charge Sheet was sent to his native place. It can well be assumed that when a person is 
performing his duty, he will be available in the colliery and during his absence he would be at his registered address 
provided in the Service Record. Though the workman was fully aware that management had issued Charge Sheet 
against him which was sent to his native village during his long absence, he did not bother to find out the indictment 
in the Charge Sheet. Management witness produced a copy of Charge Sheet as Exhibit M-land copies of Notice of 
enquiry as Exhibit M-3 and M-4. Copy of the Enquiry Proceeding is produced as Exhibit M-5 and Report of the 
Enquiry Officer is produced as Exhibit M-6. The workman has been found guilty for his absence from duty from 
9.4.993 to 20.2.995, which is more than two years which covers the entire period of his absence disclosed in the 
Charge Sheet from December 993 to 23.05.994. It is abundantly clear from the findings of the Enquiry Officer that 
the workman never showed up for duty for more than two years. It is true that the management of the employer 
company is duty bound to observe the principles of natural justice before dismissing its employee from the service of 
the company by issuing a Charge Sheet, Notice of enquiry and holding a proper enquiry proceeding. Management 
made best effort by issuing such Charge Sheet and Notice at his native place. However, this duty cast upon the 
management is not absolute in the absence of reciprocal responsibility of the employee to attend his place of work and 
either to inform the reason of absence or to seek authorization for leave on any acceptable ground. The duty of 
observing principles of natural justice by the employer has been complied and no prejudice is caused to the workman. 
In a case where the workman abandoned his duty for a long period without any information, he cannot be allowed to 
challenge the act of the management as violative of natural justice. In the instant case the management issued a 
Charge Sheet and appointed an Enquiry Officer. The Enquiry Officer in turn issued two Notice of enquiry and fixed 
two dates. The workman did not participate in the enquiry and remained absent on being chased by the money lenders, 
as disclosed in Exhibit W-3. The management after initiating a domestic enquiry on May 994 ultimately issued the 
order of dismissal on 09.0.!996. On a perusal of the order of dismissal (Exhibit W2/M-7) it appears that two Notice 
of enquiry were served upon the workman at his home address under registered post and enquiry was held on 
20.2.996 but the workman did not participate. In my considered view no prejudice was caused to the workman by 
non-issuance of second Show Cause Notice. It further appears to me that after dismissal of the workman in January 
996 the workman raised the Industrial Dispute on 26.06.202l, before the Assistant Labour Commissioner (C), 
Raniganj, Durgapur. There has been a delay of more than twenty-five (25) years in raising the Industrial Dispute after 
dismissal of the workman. The circumstances revealed that the workman has not acted in a diligent manner and his 
prayer for reinstatement after such a long period of silence is of no merit. I therefore, hold that the demand made by 
the union for reinstatement of the dismissed workman is not legally tenable and the Industrial Dispute merits dismissal 
on contest.

6. The point of contention in this case is whether the management of ECL is justified in regretting Sunny 
Mejhan’s claim for employment as dependent of her mother Binodi Mejhan. 


7. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, union representative advancing his argument submitted that after the death of Binodi 
Mejhan, her daughter informed the management about the death of her mother by letter dated 09..2009, which will 
be evident from Office Order dated 9.02.20l0 (Exhibit W-6). After deleting the name of Binodi Mejhan from the 
Roll of the company, management did not disclose the rights of the dependents in respect of the service of Binodi 
Mejhan. Initially, an application was submitted by the dependent daughter on 28.2.2009 claiming employment but it 
took some time to prepare some documents which were filed in 20l4. Mr. Kumar argued that the management held 
IME of Sunny Mejhan on 3.03.208 at the Area level where her age was decided as 35-40 years. On the basis of such 
age determined by the IME Board, the age of Sunny Mejhan was 3] years 06 months on 28.2.2009, the date of 
submitting her application for employment which was well within the upper age limit of 35 years. It is argued that 
though no dispute was raised by Sunny Mejhan against age assessed by the management a second age assessment was 
held on 3.08.2020 where her age was determined to be 40-45 years and according to such assessment, her age was 3] 
years 0 months on the date of death of her mother. The union representative strenuously argued that the dependent 
daughter is eligible for employment in place of her deceased mother as per provisions of NCWA. 


8. Mr. P.K. Das, learned advocate for the management of ECL in reply argued that no claim for employment 
was made by the dependent daughter until 24.05.20l4. The management of the company assessed the age on 
3.03.20I8 as 35-40 years and subsequently the Apex Medical Board on 3.08.2020 assessed the age as 40-45 years 
which implies that her age was more than 35 years on the date of submitting her application for employment on 
24.05.204. Learned advocate argued that management communicated the decision of the competent authority to the 
dependent daughter that she was not found fit for employment for being over age. 


9. Considered the arguments in the light of the facts and circumstances of the case, pleadings submitted, 
evidence adduced and the guiding rules. Admittedly, Binodi Mejhan, the mother of Sunny Mejhan died in harness on 
30.08.2009. According to the provisions of clause 9.3.4 of NCWA, the dependents to be considered for employment 
should be physically fit and suitable for employment and the age should not be more than 35 years. In the case of 
Sukumoni Hembram alias Sukumoni Mejhan Vs. Union of India and Others [MAT 27 of 2024] the Hon'ble 
Division Bench of High Court at Calcutta observed : 


“ NCWA is a negotiated agreement that has been arrived at between the employer and the employees. It is a 
settlement under section 2 (9) of the Industrial Disputes Act, /947 and has binding effect on the parties thereto under 
section 76 (3) of the Act of 7947. NCWA has made provisions for compassionate appointment for the dependents of 
the deceased employee. ” 


Clause 9.3.2 of NCWA-VI provides that employment would be provided to one dependent of the workman who dies 
while in service. Furthermore, Clause 9.3.4 provides that the dependents to be considered for employment should be 
physically fit and suitable for employment and their age should not be more than thirty-five (35) years provided that 
the age limit for a female spouse would be forty-five (45) years as given in Clause 9.5.0. On a close reading of 
provisions of NCWA, there is no specified time for reckoning the age of dependent for considering him/her for the 
purpose of employment. In this matter, a Circular has been issued by the management of ECL bearing No. CIL/C- 
58/83८/9.4.3/63 dated 25.07.2003 wherein it has been provided that the age on the date of submitting the 
application would be considered for offering employment on compassionate ground. Union produced a copy of an 
application, said to have been submitted by Sunny Mejhan on 28.!2.2009 addressed to the Manager, Bhanora West 
Block Colliery. The document has been marked ‘X’ for identification and it bears a receiving seal without mentioning 
the designation of the person who received it. The management of ECL claimed that application for employment was 
submitted by Sunny Mejhan for the first time on 24.05.20l4. Therefore, it needs to be considered whether the 
dependent daughter was within the age limit of 35 years on 24.05.204. 


0. The process for considering the proposal for employment was initiated as per the guidelines of the company 
and medical examination of Sunny Mejhan by the IME at the Area level was held on 3.03.20I8. The IME Board 
found her fit for employment and her age was assessed as 35-40 years on that date. Once again, she was examined by 
the Apex Medical Board on 3.08.2020 where her age was assessed as 40 to 45 years as on 3.08.2020. It has been 
contented on behalf of the management that as there was delay of more than two years in raising the claim for 
employment after the death of employee. As per circulars of ECL dated 6.03.207, IME was to be held at Sanctoria 
Hospital. Therefore, the determination of age at the Area level is not to be taken into consideration. It is urged that age 
determined by the Apex Medical Board at Sanctoria Hospital had to be relied upon and on the basis of such 
determination, the age of Sunny Mejhan was 42 years, 6 months on 3!.08.2020. Accordingly, her age on 24.05.20I4 
was 36 years, 3 months. The contrary argument of the union was that the age of Sunny Mejhan in the Service Excerpt 
report of her mother dated 0.04.987 was recorded as 7 years. Therefore, on basis of such document, the age of 
daughter would be 34 years, | month and 24 days as on the date of submitting her application on 24.05.204. It may 
be further gathered from the argument of the union that once the age of the dependent daughter was assessed at the

Area Level on 3!.03.208 and found her 35 to 40 years of age, by computing her age on the date of application, she 
would be 33 years and 8 months of age and well within the age limit for providing employment to her. I find that once 
the age was determined by the IME at the Area Level on 3.03.208 and no complaint was raised against such 
findings by the candidate, management was estopped from reassessing the age of the candidate by another Medical 
Board by the Headquarter after a period of two years and five months only to disqualify her on the ground that she 
was over age. Management appears to have delayed the process to frustrate the cause. Management cannot approbate 
and reprobate their own act to disable a person from securing her right. Therefore, I am not inclined to accept the 
subsequent age assessment of Sunny Mejhan after a lapse of two and a half years only to contradict management’s 
own finding on earlier occasion which was in favour of the candidate. Union has produced a copy of letter bearing No. 
ECL/CMD/C-6B/GM (P&IR)/2022/633 dated 2.05.2022 issued by the General Manager (P&IR), ECL addressed to 
the General Managers of Sripur and other Areas laying down guidelines for pre-employment medical examination, 
wherein it is stated that their earlier communication dated 6.03.20l7 about holding IME at Sanctoria Hospital in 
respect of cases which are beyond two years from the date of death of ex-employee stood withdrawn and henceforth 
IME of all cases would be exclusively held at the Area according to its cluster as was done before, and therefore, there 
is no need to send any person to Sanctoria Hospital for holding their IME. On a perusal of the guidelines, I find that 
though it was issued in May 2022, much after holding the second IME at the Headquarters level, the management of 
ECL was possessed with the idea of holding all IME at the Area Level instead of at the Headquarters. In view of such 
guidelines dated 2.05.2022 which was issued during pendency of this Industrial Dispute, I am of the considered view 
that the age assessed by the IME Board at the Area Level on 3.03.20I8 needs to be considered as the report 
determining the correct age of Sunny Mejhan. The decision of the competent authority relying upon the subsequent 
findings of the Apex Medical Board, contradicting the earlier assessment is found self-defeating and has no 
foundation. Thus, the same is not sustainable under the law. 


Il. This Industrial Dispute has been raised due to disqualifying Sunny Mejhan for her employment. It is found 
that the age of the dependent daughter according to the Service Excerpt of the employee and the first assessment by 
the IME brings her within the zone of consideration, so far as age is concerned. She was also found fit for 
employment. Therefore, the afterthought of the management followed by a second medical examination of the 
candidate two and a half years after her first IME is prejudicial, arbitrary, illegal and cannot be accepted. Under 
NCWA, there is no time limit for submitting application by the dependent of the deceased employee for employment 
and it is well settled in case of Sukumoni Hembram alias Sukumoni Mejhan Vs. Union of India and Others (supra). 
On the basis of my above discussion, Sunny Mejhan is entitled to employment under the management of ECL against 
the death of her mother, Binodi Mejhan. The management of ECL is directed to complete the procedural formalities 
for her employment within a period of two months from the date of communication of the Award. 


Hence, 
ORDERED

formalities within two months from the date of communication of this Award. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be

Referring to the Standard Operating Procedure of Coal India Limited dated 28.08.2023 which was duly approved in 
the 63" CMDs meeting held on 8.08.2023, it is submitted that the time limit for submitting application for 
employment was relaxed by extending such time up to 3! December 2023 and thereafter from the year 2024 the time 
limit for submitting application was only for one year from the date of death. It is argued that in the instant case 
application has been filed on 03.08.207, therefore there was no reason for not considering the application on the 
ground of delay in submission. Mr. Kumar further argued that Chunni Devi, the wife of the deceased employee being 
the head of the family had nominated Guddu Rabidas, the youngest son for employment in place of the deceased 
employee. According to the union representative the widow has the prerogative to decide as to who amongst the 
family members should get employment in place of her deceased husband. It is argued that if the widow had the right 
to decide the claim for employment of dependent, any objection raised by other siblings against the nominated 
dependent would be without force. It is urged that the management of ECL is under legal obligation to provide 
employment to Guddu Rabidas, the dependent and nominated son of the deceased employee as per the provisions of 
Clause 9.3.] of NCWA. 


3. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management of ECL, in reply argued that Umesh Rabidas, the eldest 
son of the deceased employee raised objection against the proposal for employment to his younger brother, Guddu 
Rabidas. It is argued that according to the Circular dated 3.0.2009 issued by the General Manager (P&IR), ECL it is 
essential that all the dependent members of the deceased employee, whose names appeared in the Service Record 
must submit no objection in favour of the person seeking employment. In the instant case Umesh Rabidas raised 
objection against the nomination of Guddu Rabidas, as such the management offered to pay MMCC to the widow of 
the deceased. It is further argued that due to such objection raised by another son of the deceased employee the prayer 
for employment of Guddu Rabidas is not sustainable and the Industrial Dispute is liable to be dismissed. 


4. Having considered the arguments advanced on behalf of both parties, the pleadings, evidence adduced and 
the provisions under Clause 9.3.l of NCWA-IX, I find that employment has to be provided to one dependent of the 
employee who died while in service of the company. In Clause 9.3.3 of NCWA-IX a dependent has been described 
for this purpose as a wife or a husband as the case may be, son and legally adopted son. It does not specify that the 
eldest son of the deceased employee should be considered for employment. The other essential criteria for providing 
employment as per Clause 9.3.4 of NCWA-IX is that the dependent who is considered for employment should be 
physically fit, suitable for employment and aged not more than 35 years provided that the age limit in case of female 
spouse would be 45 years as given in Clause 9.5.0. There is no dispute over the fact that Dukhi Rabidas died in 
harness on 3.05.20I5, leaving behind Chunni Devi, his widow, three sons namely, Umesh Rabidas, Ramavali 
Rabidas, and Guddu Rabidas and four daughters namely Gouri Devi, Pravila Devi, Manita Devi and Kanchan Devi. 
From the evidence on record, it is clear that Chunni Devi nominated her youngest son for employment as a dependent 
in place of her deceased husband. The application was initially submitted by her on 03.08.207 (Exhibit W-4). The 
management in response to her letter issued letter No. 096 dated 09/I.0.207 (Exhibit W-5), requesting her to 
submit complete employment file with “No Objection” from all the dependent family members as per Clause 9.4.0 of 
NCWA-IX. It is admitted by the management that on !5.0.2020 Guddu Rabidas submitted all the documents along 
with application of Chunni Devi and “No Objection” from other family members (Exhibit W-7). The management of 
ECL having received such application should have acted upon the same by considering the prayer for employment. It 
has been argued on behalf of the management that Umesh Rabidas, the eldest son of the deceased employee submitted 
an objection against the prayer for employment (Exhibit W-8/M-6) due to which management was unable to consider 


[भाग Ive 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 585 


the prayer for employment. On a close reading of the provision of Clause 9.4.0 of NCWA-IX, I found that there is no 
mandatory requirement of submitting NOC by all the family members of the deceased employee in favour of the 
dependent claiming employment. In the instant case Chunni Devi, the principal dependent of the deceased employee 
has clearly stated in her affidavit-in-chief, supporting the case of the union in their written statement that Umesh 
Rabidas was not a dependent and was living separately from the family of the deceased employee. It is also gathered 
from the evidence of Guddu Rabidas that Umesh Rabidas was running a business in the style of General Store at his 
native place, which has been established. Such evidence has not been controverted. Therefore, the management is 
dutybound to consider the option exercised by the dependent of the deceased employee and not impose their view of 
providing alternative relief of MMCC, which is usually opted by the spouse when she is more than forty-five years of 
age and has no dependent to take up employment on behalf of the family of the deceased. In the instant case all four 
married daughters of the deceased employee as well as the widow have expressed their support in favour of Guddu 
Rabidas, seeking employment as a dependent of their deceased father. The management of Parascole Colliery is not in 
a position to dispute the claim on the ground of delayed submission of application for employment as there has been a 
relaxation of time limit up to 3.2.2023 for submission of application as per the Standard Operating Procedure under 
NCWA dated 8.08.2023. The evidence on record clearly brings out the fact that Guddu Rabidas, the younger son has 
been nominated by the widow of the deceased employee who is the principal dependent and reposed faith upon the 
dependent son as a person who would take care of family responsibilities and did not support the objection raised by 
the other two sons, namely Umesh Rabidas and Ramavali Rabidas. In view of the fact and circumstances of this case I 
hold that the management is under a legal obligation to consider the prayer for employment of Guddu Rabidas as a 
dependent son of Dukhi Rabidas as per the provisions of Clause 9.3.l of NCWA-IX and complete the employment 
procedure within two (2) months from the date of communication of the Award. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest in favour of Guddu Rabidas, the dependent son of the 
deceased employee Dukhi Rabidas. The management of Parascole Colliery under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields 
Limited is directed to consider the prayer for employment of Guddu Rabidas and complete the employment procedure 
within two (2) months from the date of communication of the Award. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above 
findings. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for 
information and Notification.

one Latli Devi @ Tejni Devi claiming herself to be the second wife of Ch. Jagu Das. The management issued a letter 
to the Dy. Chief Personnel Manager, Kajora Area dated 08.05.2006 informing that Tejni Devi has raised objection 
against providing employment to Dhapru Das in place of Ch. Jagu Das. According to the workman witness Tejni Devi 
is not the second wife of Ch. Jagu Das and her name has not been recorded as his wife even after the death of his 
mother. It appears from Exhibit W-6, which is a copy of Form PS-4, relating to nomination in respect of service 
benefits of Ch. Jagu Das that the name of Jumni Devi has been recorded as nominee and described as the wife with 
hundred percent (00%) share. Therefore, the management of ECL should not have entertained the complaint of Tejni 
Devi to stop the employment process as her claim had no legal foundation and the documents in the custody of the 
management of ECL could not have accommodated such extraneous claim. To set the dispute at rest Dhapru Das 
submitted a copy of judgement of acquittal passed by the learned District and Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 
I, Giridih in Criminal Appeal No. 46/20l0 (Exhibit W-) dated 3.03.204, setting aside an order passed by the 
Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Giridih on 20.05.200, where Dhapru Das had been held guilty under Section 
498(A) of the Indian Penal Code. The management of ECL by any competent court was never impleaded in any civil 
suit nor was there any order of restrainment against the management of ECL preventing it from providing employment 
to the son of deceased employee on the basis of the NCWA. The criminal case in which the petitioner son was 
entangled was finally disposed of in the year 204 but the management remained silent for seven long years to add to 
the delay and did not carry out its solemn responsibility of honouring the provisions of NCWA in its true perspective. 
The manner in which the prayer of Dhapru Das was delt with by different tiers of management of ECL only reveals 
their deliberate act of delaying the matter to frustrate and exhaust the claim for which the petitioner son is not 
responsible in any manner. It was only on 26.02.202l the Chief Manager, Kajora Area, issued a letter bearing No. 
ECL/CKC/P&IR/C-6/202/55 (Exhibit W-3) to Dhapru Das, informing that the employment proposal has been 
examined by the Competent Authority and observed as follows : 


“ The aforementioned employment proposal of Sri Dhapru das has been examined and it is found that the 
appointment of compassionate ground is given only to help a family to tide over the stringent financial crisis resulting 
from the sudden death of employee. 


Whereas, in this case, family members of the ex- employee indulged themselves in to their internal dispute 
which was ultimately dragged themselves in to court and a substantial period of about 768 years is now over. 
Therefore, essence of compassionate appointment is defeated in this case. 


Further, it is observed that, candidate is trying to procure employment as a matter of right. 


Whereas, Honorable Court had held that appointment on compassionate ground cannot be claimed as matter 
of right.” 


It needs to be born in mind that there is a presumption of innocence in favour of a person even when he is facing a 
criminal charge in a trial. It is only after he is convicted, an inference can be drawn against him. In the present case 
simply by lodging a complaint against Dhapru Das cannot stall the proceeding for his employment as per provisions 
of NCWA. The legal right of a dependent which has arisen out of the provision of NCWA cannot be curtailed on the 
basis of a complaint before the Criminal Court. In order to bank upon a contention that a family dispute prevailed with 
counter claims in respect of the service claimed by one of the dependents of deceased employee, the management 
should be in a position to establish that a Civil dispute had been initiated against the claimant as well as the 
management of the company, raising objection against such claim. In the present case management has relied upon a 
decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of M/s. Eastern Coalfields Ltd Vs. Anil Badyakar and 
Others [Civil Appeal No. 3597 of 2009], wherein the Hon’ble Apex Court held : 


atic the compassionate appointment is not a vested right which can be exercised at any time in future. The 
compassionate employment cannot be claimed and offered after a lapse of time and after the crisis is over. In the 
instant case the employee died in harness in the year /967 and after a long squabble by the dependents of the 
deceased, they arrived at a settlement that the son-in-law of the second daughter who is unemployed may request for 
appointment on compassionate grounds. The request so made was accepted by the Personal Manager of the Company 
subject to the approval of the Director of the Company. The Director (P), who is the competent authority for post 
facto approval, keeping in view the object and purpose of providing compassionate appointment has cancelled the 
provisional appointment on the ground that nearly after 72 years from the date of death of the employee such an 
appointment could not have been offered to the so called dependent of the deceased employee. In our considered view, 
the decision of the employer was in consonance with Umesh Kumar Nagpal’s case and the same should not have been 
interfered with by the High Court.” 


ll. The facts of the present case is distinguishable from the facts of the case relied upon by the management of 
ECL. In the instant case Dhapru Das, the dependent son submitted his application claiming employment against the 
death of his father as per provisions of Clause 9.3.! of NCWA. Such claim was made within two months from the date 
of death of his father. There is no dispute that he is a dependent of the deceased employee and his name appeared as 
son in the Service Record Excerpt and the family particulars of the deceased employee for which such documents are 
maintained. The screening and medical examination of the candidate was also carried out within a reasonable period 
and documents were submitted. The stage was set for final consideration of the claim for employment when on the 


[भाग I—davs 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 59] 


basis of a complaint submitted by Tejni Devi, management thought it wise not to proceed further in processing the 
claim for employment. Management representatives did not apply their mind that Tejni Devi did not figure in the 
Service Record of the deceased employee at any point of time. Therefore, management acted in a grossly illegal and 
arbitrary manner by entertaining the claim of Tejni Devi and thereby deprived the dependent son of the deceased 
employee from his rightful claim for employment for nearly 20 years. In the case of Anil Badyakar and Others 
(Supra.) there was a long dispute against the dependents of the deceased employee leading to delay in submitting 
claim for employment. The circumstances in this case is entirely different. Therefore, I hold that the ratio of the 
decision relied upon by the management does not apply to the facts and circumstances of this case. 


2. In the case of Sukumoni Hembram alias Sukumoni Mejhan Vs. Union of India and Others [MAT 27 of 
2024] the Hon’ble Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court at Calcutta held : 


“ NCWA is a negotiated agreement that has been arrived at between the employer and the employees. It is a 
settlement under section 2 (p) of the Industrial Disputes Act, /947 and has binding effect on the parties thereto under 
section 76 (3) of the Act of /947. NCWA has made provisions for compassionate appointment for the dependents of 
the deceased employee.” The Hon'ble High Court further held that none of the clauses 9.3.0 to 9.5.0 of NCWA 
provide any time limit for applying or prescribe any financial solvency of the family as a disqualification. It does not 
allow the employer to choose between the dependents as to who it would grant the employment or the MMCC. The 
position of law is clearly settled that a claim for employment under NCWA is not treated as a compassionate 
appointment, depending upon the financial status of the family of the deceased employee. Nowhere, in the NCWA it 
has been stated that such employment was been provided only to the dependents to tide over sudden crisis resulting 
due to sudden death of the bread-earner or only in cases where the family of the deceased is in a penury. The terms of 
providing employment have gone beyond such consideration and has only specified the eligible age and physical 
fitness of the candidate to be considered for the employment. In order to turn down the claim for employment of a 
dependent on the ground that there has been lapse of time and the sudden crisis due to the death of the employee is 
over, the provisions of NCWA needs to be revised and necessary changes should be incorporated before regretting the 
prayer for employment on the ground of delay. From the factual matrix of this case, I find that the delay has been 
caused at the instance of the management by stalling the proceeding on the basis of frivolous complaint from a person 
who does not figure as a family member of the deceased in the Service Record. Since the delay in finalizing the claim 
for employment can be attributed to the management, the dependent son is not liable to suffer the loss. Therefore, I 
hold that the decision of the management communicated through their letter dated 26.02.202l / 06.03.202 are not 
legally tenable. This is an appropriate case where the management of ECL shall be directed to provide employment to 
Dhapru Das after completing the process of employment within two months from the date of communication of the 
Award. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against the management of Lachipur Colliery under Kajora 
Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited. The management of Eastern Coalfields Limited is directed to provide 
employment to Dhapru Das, the dependent son of Late Ch. Jagu Das, ex-employee of Eastern Coalfields Limited after 
completing the formalities related to employment within two months form the date of communication of the Award. 
Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry 
of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for information and Notification.

i. As per Ex W-4 dated 02.0.2003, the Chief Manager, Zonal Office has addressed a note to the Chief 
Manager (PER & HRD) dated 02.0.2003 furnishing the name of the I Party as the one and only temporary / 
daily wage employee who has completed 240 days of service in a calendar year continuously from 0.08.992 
and his aggregate qualifying temporary service / daily wage service as 0 years 0l month and 20 days as on 
30.09.2002. 


2. Ex W-5 copy of the statement of appointments made on daily wages for the month of January 2005 
dated 02.02.2005 shows the name of the I Party under the designation scavenger with aggregate temporary 
service of 3 years 0 month and 22 days with date of appointment as 0.08.992 for cleaning of toilets at Office 
and Bank House. This piece of evidence goes diametrically opposite to the oral testimony of MW | denying 
WW t having performed the work of scavenger in the II Party Bank. 


3. Ex W-6 accompanied with Ex W-7 is an intimation from the Chief Manager (OA) to the Chief 
Manager (PER & HRD) dated 2.07.2005 revealing that the services of the I party continued to be used on 
payment of 3/4" wages by debit to charges A/c (Salaries and allowances). 


4. Ex W-8 dated 6.08.2005 an internal communication from the Zonal Office to the Chief Manager 
(PER & HRD) is also on similar lines. Ex W-9 issued by the General Manager to the Deputy General Manager, 
Hubli, dated .05.2006 reveals that the I Party has completed more than 240 days of service during the year 
994 onwards and hence he becomes a protected employee in terms of the Industrial Dispute Act, however 
making the Bank’s stand clear that there is no question of considering his permanent absorption and also 
requiring to some action against the Officials in retaining him as a temporary sweeper for such a long period. 
At no stretch of imagination it could be assumed that the I Party would be normally blessed with copy of such 
an internal communication at the instance of the officials of the II Party; instead procuration of Ex W-9 would 
only be by way of hooks and crooks by the I Party himself. 


5. Ex W-0 is the application submitted by the I party before the ALC(C), Hubli, raising a dispute 
seeking conciliation dated 6.06.208. In Ex W-] statement submitted by the management before the 
ALC(C), Hubbli, duration of the service of the I Party is confirmed till 3.03.208 in the lunch room of the 
Administrative Office of the Respondent Bank with reference to the Attendance marked by him. Under Ex W- 
I dated 5..208, the management expressed its agreement to pay wages approved to him from 0.2.207 
to 3.03.20I8 and the same is sought to be recorded in the proceedings of settlement. Ex W-2 is the 
proceedings before the ALC(C) dated 5..208 advising the management to make payments to the I Party as 
per Payment of Wages Act and Payment of Bonus Act on or before 22..20I8 under intimation to the said 
office. Eventual consequence is reflected in Ex W-3 report submitted by the II Party management revealing 
credit of Rs. 89,400.00 towards the total wages of I Party for the period from 0.2.207 to 07.06.208 and Rs. 
2,000.00 towards the bonus for the period 0.04.20I5 to 3.03.206, 0.04.206 to 3.03.20I7 and from 
0.04.207 to 3.03.208, totaling to Rs. ,0,400.00 towards his SB Account bearing No. 04676394 with the 
II Party bank at Hubli Main Branch. The said payment is illustrated in Ex W-23 passbook for the relevant 
period. 


6. As per Ex W-7, the management offered a sum of Rs. 78,095.00 as retrenchment compensation and 
Rs. 4,544.00 as one month’s notice period wages to the I Party without prejudice to its contention in the 
conciliation proceedings and requested the Conciliation Officer to conclude the conciliation proceedings and to 
record settlement for a total amount of Rs. 2,03,039.00 along with tables of calculation under the respective 
heads. None of the records produced in evidence reveal that the said amount offered by the management has 
been blissfully accepted by the I Party ever during the conciliation proceedings. In the light of the documentary 
evidence discussed above, there is no basis for the stand of denial adopted by MW | relating to the continuous 
services proved to have been rendered by the I Party in the IT Party Bank. 


7. Ex W-I8 is the proceedings before the ALC(C), Hubli, the Conciliation Officer recording failure of 
conciliation and issuance of certificate accordingly as per the request of the I Party. 

8. Eventually this petition is filed under Section 2(a)2 by the I Party. The documents referred to and 
discussed above evidently indicate continuous service of the I party for a pretty good period of duration 
commencing from 992. Apparently his service under the II Party came to a standstill in the year 208. Entire 


[भाग W—davs 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 597 


wage arrears, as already observed, stood cleared off under Ex W-3 in addition to the bonus upto then. So 
ample evidence is there on record establishing that the I Party workman has performed continuous service 
under the II Party for years together while the mandatory requisite obliging the II Party to perform its 
statutory duties towards the workman is only 240 days of service of the workman. Therefore it can be safely 
inferred that the termination of the I Party from service in early June 208 without giving notice of 
retrenchment, one month notice pay and retrenchment compensation is strictly in violation of the provisions of 
Section 25F of the Act. It is profitable to extract Section 25F from the statute in this context. It reads: 


Section 25F: 
Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen. 


- No workman employed in any industry who has been in continuous service for not less than one 
year under an employer shall be retrenched by that employer until- 


(a)the workman has been given one month 's notice in writing indicating the reasons for retrenchment and 
the period of notice has expired, or the workman has been paid in lieu of such notice, wages for the period 
of the notice:[* * *] [ Proviso omitted by Act 49 of /9०84, Section 32 (w.e.f. 8.8.984).] 


(b)the workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which shall be equivalent to 
fifteen days 'average pay [for every completed year of continuous service] [ Substituted by Act 36 of 964, 
Section 4, for " for every completed year of service" (w.e.f. 9.2.964).] or any part thereof in excess of 
six months; and 


(c)notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate Government [or such authority as may be 
specified by the appropriate Government by notification in the Official Gazette.] [ Inserted by Act 36 of 
964, Section 4 (w.e.f. 9.2.964).] 


It is equally clear that retrenchment / termination of the I Party did occur not on account of any fault on its 
part as no such contention rather allegation is put forth against him by the II Party but purely a unilateral 
decision of the Employer. In the afore discussed factual scenario, such unilateral action by the II Party does 
not stand justified by any reason. 


9. As on the date of examination of the I Party as WW l, his age is shown to be 55 years before this 
Tribunal. Necessarily he stood superannuated in the year 2024. One of the reliefs sought in the claim petition 
is reinstatement to service with full backwages, continuity of service, regular pay scales, regularization and 
ancillary benefits from the date of his appointment. Since the I Party has already superannuated as he attained 
60 years in the year 2024, no question of his reinstatement into service does arise. All the same the law stands 
in guard to protect his rights prescribing that the workman who has attained the age of superannuation can be 
awarded backwages if his termination or dismissal is found to be illegal, wrongful or unjustified. In the 
aforesaid discussion it is amply found that the termination of the I Party from the service is illegal, wrongful 
and unjustified. So much so, while reinstatement is not feasible in respect of him as he has already reached the 
retirement age, this tribunal can award backwages with continuity of service for the purpose of calculating his 
consequential benefits viz., Bonus and Gratuity, from the date of termination till the date of superannuation. 


20. Since the termination of the I Party is found illegal, unfair and inoperative since the provisions of 
Section 25F are violated by the Employer, and not on the fault of the I Party, he is entitled for full back wages. 
Since Ex W-7 shows the one month’s notice period wage as Rs. 4,544.00 payable to the I Party, the 
backwages found payable by the Employer to the I Party is to be counted at Rs. 4,544.00 per month from the 
date of his termination till the date of superannuation. Along with full backwages, the I Party is entitled for 
getting the benefit of continuity of service for the purpose of calculating his consequential benefits viz., Bonus 
for the rest of the period i.e., from 0/04/208 and Gratuity as well. Such continuity of service is countable for 
calculating PF also if found eligible in a proceeding if any initiated there on. Since full backwages is counted 
for the duration of his deemed service w.e.f. the date of his termination, I am not inclined to grant him a 
further amount of retrenchment compensation, just to prevent an unjust enrichment or double benefit for the 
same period. 


2i. With this view the discussions on this issue are concluded drawing the finding indicated above and the 
following Award is passed. 
AWARD 
The Petition is allowed in part granting full backwages to the I Party @ Rs. 4,544.00 (Rupees Fourteen 
Thousand Five Hundred Forty Four only) per month from the date of his termination till the date of 
superannuation on attaining 60 years of age with continuity of service for the purpose of : 
(i) Calculating consequential benefits of Bonus from 0.04.208 to the date of superannuation; 
(ii) Calculating Gratuity from August 992 till the date of his superannuation, if not already paid by the 
II Party and; 


(iii) for calculating Provident Fund as well, if found eligible in a proceeding if any, initiated there 
on.

The proposed amendments to the Articles of Association (“AOA”) of National Stock Exchange of India Limited (“NSEIL”)

inviting objection/suggestion/criticism, if any, from persons likely to be affected. Pursuant thereto, the Securities and 
Exchange Board of India (“SEBI’) has vide its letter no. HO/47/25/ll  (2)2026-MRD-RAC2/I/548/2026 
dated February 8, 2026, taken on record the amendments to the AOA of NSEIL as stipulated therein. The AOA amended 
hereunder shall stand effective from the date of its publication in the Gazette of India or Gazette of State of Maharashtra, 
whichever is later. 


The existing AOA was formulated in accordance with the provisions of the erstwhile Companies Act, 956. Considering the 
various amendments made to the applicable laws, regulations, rules, guidelines from time to time, there is a need to amend 
the Existing AOA in order to align it with the prevailing provisions of Schedule I, Table F of the Companies Act, 203 (‘the 
Act’), the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 205 
(“Listing Regulations”), the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 20l8 (“ICDR Regulations”), the Securities Contracts (Regulation) (Stock Exchanges and Clearing 
Corporations) Regulations, 20l8 (“SECC Regulations”) and other applicable laws, regulations, rules, guidelines each as 
amended from time to time, few provisions have been incorporated in the amended AOA by way of inserting and/or omitting 
and/or substituting the existing Headings /Title / sub-headings, Articles and its Clauses with altered revised and/or new 
Headings / sub-headings, Articles and its Clauses.

expressly provided for in these Articles. In the event of any inconsistency or repugnancy between these Articles and

thereto, and the Rules made thereunder, as amended from time to time (hereinafter collectively referred to as the “Act’’).

S.R.O. 9.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, the President 
hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the posts of Senior Armament Store Officer 
and Armament Store Officer (Group ‘A’ and ‘B’ posts) in Indian Navy, Ministry of Defence, namely :- 


l. Short Title and Commencement .— (l) These rules may be called the Ministry of Defence, Indian Navy, 
Senior Armament Store Officer and Armament Store Officer, (Group ‘A’ and ‘B’ posts) Recruitment Rules, 2026. 

(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 

2. Application .— These rules shall apply to the posts as specified in column (L) of the Schedule annexed to these 
tules. 

3. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix .— The number of the said posts, their classification 


and level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these 
tules. 


4. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualification, etc _ The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications 
and other matters relating to the said posts shall be as specified in columns (5) to ((3) of the said Schedule. 


5. Initial Constitution —(a)All existing incumbents holding the post of Assistant Armament Supply Officer on 
regular basis and promoted from Senior Store Superintendent before the commencement of these rules shall be deemed 
to have been appointed as Armament Store Officer from the date from which they were regularly appointed to the post 
of Assistant Armament Supply Officer on commencement of these rules . 


(b) All existing incumbents holding the post of Junior Time Scale of Indian Naval Armament Service on regular 
basis and promoted from Store stream of Naval Armament Organisation before the commencement of these rules shall 
be deemed to have been appointed as Senior Armament Store Officer from the date from which they were regularly 
appointed to the post of Junior Time Scale of Indian Naval Armament Service on commencement of these rules. 


(c) Existing incumbents in the post of Senior Store Superintendent before the commencement of these rules will 
cease to be considered in the feeder grade for promotion to the post of Assistant Armament Supply Officer on 
commencement of these rules. 


6. Disqualification .— No person,— 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or

in this regard.

may be by order for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any 
class or category of persons.

to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the other Backward Classes, Ex-servicemen and other 
special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in 
this regard.

(Civil/Mechanical/Electrical) and Assistant Engineer (Civil/Mechanical/Electrical), (Group (87 post) Recruitment 
Rules, 204, in so far as they relate to the post of Junior Engineer (Civil), Junior Engineer (Electrical) and Junior 
Engineer(Mechanical), except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President 
hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the posts of Junior Engineer(Civil), Junior 
Engineer(Electrical) and Junior Engineer(Mechanical), in the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Department of Water Resources, 
River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Farakka Barrage Project, namely:- 

l. Short title and commencement.— () These rules may be called the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Department of 
Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Farakka Barrage Project, Junior 
Engineer(Civil), Junior Engineer(Electrical) and Junior Engineer(Mechanical), Group- ‘B’ Post Recruitment 
Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Application.- These rules shall apply to the posts specified in column (l) of the Schedule annexed to these 
tules. 
3. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix. - The number of the said posts, their classification 


and level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the said Schedule. 


4. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.— The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications 
and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to ((3) of the said Schedule. 


5. Disqualification. — No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 


shall be eligible for appointment to the said posts:

S.O. 329.—Whereas by notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural 
Gas S.O.No.3575(E) dated the 3].07.2025, issued under sub-section (l) of section 3 of the Petroleum and Minerals 
Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 962 (50 of 962), (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), 
published in the Extra Ordinary Gazette of India dated the 04.08.2025, the Government of India declared its intention 
to acquire the Right of User in the land specified in the Schedule appended to that notification for the purpose of 
laying pipeline for transportation of Natural Gas through Silchar CGD Spur line of Guwahati - Shillong - Silchar - 
Panisagar Section of North - East Natural Gas Pipeline in the state of Assam by Indradhanush Gas Grid 
Limited (IGGL). 


And whereas copies of the said Extraordinary Gazette notification were made available to the public. 


And whereas the objections received from the public to the laying of the pipeline have been considered and 
disposed by the Competent Authority. 


And whereas the Competent Authority has, under sub-section (l) of section 6 of the said Act submitted its 
report to the Government of India. 


And whereas the Government of India after considering the said report and on being satisfied that the said 
land is required for laying the pipeline, has decided to acquire right of user therein; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (.) of the section 6 of the said Act, the 
Government of India hereby declares that the right of user in the land specified in the Schedule appended to this 
notification is hereby acquired for laying the pipeline; 


And further, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 6 of the said Act, the 
Government of India hereby directs that the Right of User in the land for laying the pipeline shall, instead of vesting 
in Government of India, vest, on this date of the publication of the declaration, in the Indradhanush Gas Grid Limited 
(IGGL), free from all encumbrances.

और उक्त राजपत्रित अधिसूचना की प्रतियाँ जनता को उपलब्ध करा दी गई थी; 
और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने जनता से प्राप्त आक्षेपों को परीक्षण के उपरांत निपटान कर दिया है; 


और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 6 की उप - धारा (() के अधीन भारत सरकार को अपनी 
रिपोर्ट दे दी है; 


और भारत सरकार ने, उक्त रिपोर्ट पर विचार करने के पश्चात और यह संतुष्ट हो जाने पर कि उक्त भूमि 
पाइपलाइन बिछाने के लिए अपेक्षित है, उसमें उपयोग के अधिकार का अर्जन करने का विनिश्चय किया है; 


अतःअब, भारतसरकार, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 6 कि उपधारा (॥) द्वारा प्रदत शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते SA, 
यह घोषणा करती है कि इस अधिसूचना से संलग्न अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि में पाइपलाइन बिछाने के लिए उपयोग के 
अधिकार का अर्जन किया जाता है; 


और भारत सरकार, उक्त अधिनियम कि धारा 6 कि उपधारा (4) द्वारा प्रदत शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुये, यह 
निर्देश देती है कि पाइपलाइने बिछाने के लिए भूमि मे उपयोग के अधिकार, इस घोषणा के प्रकाशन की तारीख को, भारत 
सरकार में निहित होने के बजाय, पाइपलाइन बिछाने का प्रस्ताव करने वाली मैसर्सइंद्रधनुषगैसग्रिडलिमिटेड में निहित 
होगा और तदुपरि, भूमि में ऐसे उपयोग का अधिकार, इस प्रकार अधिरोपित निबंधनों और शर्तों के अधीन रहते हुये, सभी 
विलंगमों से मुक्त, मैसर्सइंद्रधनुषगैसग्रिडलिमिटेड में निहित होगा।

dispute between the employers, in relation to the managementof State Bank of Indiaand the Union of State Bank 
Karmachari Sena, (Nagpur Module), for adjudication, as per No. L-20/39/207 (IR(B-D) dated 0.02.208, with 
the following schedule: - 


“Whether action of the management of State Bank of India, Local Head Office, Mumbai through its 
Chief General Manager and State Bank of India Zonal Office, Zone-I, Nagpur Through its Dy. 
General Manager to implement the transfers under redeployment policy without taking into 
consideration the data of branch wise access/ shortage staff along with the criteria adopted to arrive at 
such figure as well as the appointment of the new recruits and merger of associate banks in State Bank 
of India is fair, just or legal? If not, to what relief the concerned Unionis entitled to? And what are the 
other directions necessary in the matter? 


2. Case is called out. Learned counsel for the respondent Shri. Dadu Sachadeva is present before the court but 
no one is present on behalf of petitioner despite service of notice. On the previous date learned counsel for the Party 
No. 2, Mr. Marpakwar has filed a pursis wherein he has mentioned that despite repeated attempts to contact by a 
phone calls and latter to client he has failed to provide necessary instructions to proceed further in the present matter. 
In these circumstances, he has withdrawn his power on the previous date. From perusal of record, it is apparent that 
this reference has been received to this court on 6.02.20l8. Although Statement of Claim and Written Statement as 
well as rejoinder have been filed by the parties respectively but no evidence has been filed by the petitioner to prove 
his case. Therefore, it appears that petitioner is not interested to contest the case further more. No other evidence has 
been filed by the petitioner to prove the contents of the claim. Claim of the petitioner is not proved.So, it is closed. 


Hence, it is ordered.

The Central Government, Ministry of Labour & Employment vide its Order No. L-14011/15/2018-IR(DU) 
dated 27.11.2018 referred the following Industrial Dispute to this Tribunal for adjudication. 


Con..2 
The schedule mentioned in that order is: 


“Whether the action of the management of Indian Coast Guard, Base Maintenance Unit, Chennai, in 
transferring Sh. P. Ayan Arul Raj, Radio/Radar Fitter to [CGS Mandapam in an non-existing post at ICGS 
Mandapam is legal and justified? If not, to what relief Sh. P.Ayan Arul Raj, Radio/Radar Fitter is entitled 
to?” 


As per the claim statement the petitioner is an Indian Coast Guard Civilian Employees Union, registered under the 
Trade Union Act, 1926 was formed primarily to protect the interest of the workmen and for the welfare of the 
employees apart from maintaining harmonious relationship with the Management. It is submitted that there are 60 
civilian workmen in the establishment and most of them are members of the Union, this being the only union 


4060 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 9, 2026/VAISAKHA 19, 1948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


functioning in the establishment to espouse the cause of the workmen. It is submitted that the Union raised an 
Industrial Dispute before the Assistant Labour Commissioner (C) by letter dated 21.11.2017 under Section 2(K) of 
the Industrial Dispute Act,1947 over the issue relating to the unfair labour practices adopted by the respondent 
Management. It is submitted that the union was registered on 07.07.2017 vide Regn. No.508/TVR under the Trade 
Unions Act, 1947 and thereafter in the General Body Meeting the office bearers were elected. It is submitted that the 
fact relating to the registration of the union and the list of elected office bearers was communicated to the respondent 
Management by letter No.ICGEU/BMU/01/2017, dated 15.07.2017. 


2. It is submitted that the 1 respondent has framed the “Transfer Policy-Civilian” by letter no.CP/0518 dated 
22.11.2006 and circulated to the Regional Commanders for compliance. Para 4(c) deals with Group ‘B’ ‘C’ ‘D’ 
Non-Gazetted personal, wherein it is clearly stated that postings and transfer of these employees are to be kept at 
absolute minimum level keeping in view the administrative requirement and need for manning the posts at various 
stations. It has also been clearly mentioned that in case of transfers being inescapable, volunteers for the postings or 
transfer will be called. As far as possible only volunteers will be transferred to these vacancies. It has also been 
clearly stated that as far as possible the group ‘C’ and ‘D’ employee should not be transferred over long distance 
and efforts should be made to accommodate them near their choice station to the extent possible. 


3. As per the above, Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj was elected as Treasurer of the union. Since the Respondent / 
Management was against the formation of the union, the employee Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj was relieved and directed 
to report for duty at ICGS, Mandapam by letter No.CP/277/17, dated 31.10.2017 


4. The transfer order dated 20.10.2017 was not served on the workman till date. While the petitioner union requested 
that Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj be declared a protected workman, but the Management swiftly reacted by transferring 
Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj and victimized him by adopting unfair labour practice. Hence requested the following relief. 


i) To declare that the transfer order bearing no.1340 dated 20.10.2017 issued by the 37 Respondent 
transferring Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj, Radio/Radar Fitter from Basic Maintenance Unit, Chennai to Indian Coast 
Guard Station, Mandapam is not justified as per the guidelines laid down by the 1“ respondent in the Transfer 
Policy CP/0518 dated 22.11.2006 


ii) And to pass such other award/order as this Hon’ble Central Government Industrial Tribunal-cum-Labour 
Court may deem fit and necessary in the circumstances of the case and thus render justice.

5. The respondent in its reply stated that the Indian Coast Guard Civilian Employees Union has not been recognized 
by the Ministry of Defence, as per CGHA letter WE/0302/Welfare dated 09.10.2019.The transfer order of the three 
(3) civilian personal was promulgated vide CGRHQ(E) letter 1340 dated 20.10.17. Accordingly, the individual was 
relieved from Basic Maintenance Unit, Chennai to report at Indian Coast Guard Station, Madapam as per the 
transfer policy and pleaded that the petition be dismissed as devoid of merit. 


6. The Respondent filed the following documents in support of their contention 


Exhibit No. Date Description 

Ex.M1 18.04.2018 Nature of duties carried out by Indian Coast Guard Base 
Maintenance Unit (Chennai)

7. Heard both learned counsel and perused the records. The point arised for determination is whether the transfer of 
Shri P. Ayan Aurl Raj, Radio/Radar Fitter as ICGS, Mandapam is an not existing post at ICGS, Mandapam is legal 
and justify? If not, what relief is Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj, Radio/Radar fitter is entitled to? 


8. The claimant in its claim statement stated that the following points regarding the transfer policy. 


(a) Posting and transfer are to be kept at the absolute minimum level 
(b) Volunteers for the postings of the transfer called and will be transferred 
(c) Group ‘C’ and ‘D’ employees should not be transferred over long distance 


9. In petition claim the hardships caused to transferring described as under 


(a) Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj was transferred during October,2017 quite impossible for getting admission for his 
school going children at the new station 

(b) The workman unable to shift his family in the midst of the academic year 

(c) The employee kept the family in Chennai for his child to complete the studies in the academic year but the 
Estate Office, CPWD directed him to vacate the quarters and threatened to impose a penalty 

(d) The employee Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj fell sick because of the mental agony and remains on leave on medical 
ground from 1.11.2017 to 28.6.2018 

(e) When the workman reported for duty on 29.06.2018 at the Mandapam station, the 31 Respondent directed 


him to report for duty in Chennai for four days in a week. 


10. On perusal of whole the claim statement, the claimant nowhere stated that Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj was transferred 
to a non-existing post at ICGS Mandapam. On perusal of the claim statement, it appears that the Respondent did not 
violate the transfer policy, as the Mandapam station is not far away from Chennai station. 


11. It is the fundamental duty of transferring employee to seek the permission to overstay at Govt. accommodation by 
mentioning the sufficient reasons for occupation of the allotted house. In claim petition this facts nowhere mention 
that any application mentioning sufficient reasons for over staying at the allotted house was made or not. In this 
situation it can be presumed that no application was made by the transferring employee to the authority. 
Transferring employee Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj fails to submit the medical certificates which might have established 
the genuine grounds of his absence due to medical reasons. 


12. It is stated in the claim petition that the employee was transferred due to his involvement in the union, but the 
claimant fails to submit any evidence that may establish this fact that respondent had showed its jealous against the 
employee. The only vague reason given is that he was an elected as an office bearer in the union, the transfer of an 
employee do not appear as a result of his election to the union. 


13. The claimant has stated that no transfer order was provided to the transferred employee and that only a relieving 
order was provided to the transferee employee. The relieving order issued to Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj dated 
31.10.2017 is available at page no.2 of the paper book in this document, it is mentioned clearly that the Competent 
Authority has approved the transfer of Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj with a direction to report at ICGS Mandapam by 
10.11.2017. The relieving order was issued by the Section Officer in compliance with the order passed by the 
Competent Authority hence, no right of the transfree employee was violated by not providing a separate transfer 
order. 


14. As per the discussion above, the transfer order was not made by the Respondent in violation of transfer policy or 
against the non-existing post, it also not proved that this order was made due to desirous wish of the respondent. 


AWARD 
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner union is dismissed. The reference is answered accordingly.

support of his case. 


Thus, in view of the above said facts and the law as laid by the Hon'ble High Court in the case of V. K. Raj Industries 
v. Labour Court (1) and others 1981 (29) FLR 194 as under: 


“It is well settled that if a party challenges the legality of an order, the burden lies upon him to prove 
illegality of the order and if no evidence is produced the party invoking jurisdiction of the Court must fail. 
Whenever a workman raises a dispute challenging the validity of the termination of service if is imperative 
for him to file written statement before the Industrial Court setting out grounds on which the order is 
challenged and he must also produce evidence to prove his case. If the workman fails to appear or to file 
written statement or produce evidence, the dispute referred by the State Government cannot be answered in 
favour of the workman and he would not be entitled to any relief.” 


In the case of M/s Uptron Powertronics Employees’ Union, Ghaziabad through its Secretary v. Presiding Officer, 
Labour Court (I), Ghaziabad and others 2008 (118) FLR 1164 Hon’ble Allahabad High Court has held as under: 


“The law has been settled by the Apex Court in case of Shanker Chakravarti v. Britannia Biscuit Co. Ltd., 
V.K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court and Ors., Airtech Private Limited v. State of U.P. and Ors. 1984 (49) 
FLR 38 and Meritech India Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Ors. 1996 FLR that in the absence of any evidence led 
by or on behalf of the workman the reference is bound to be answered by the court against the workman. In 
such a situation it is not necessary for the employers to lead any evidence at all. The obligation to lead 
evidence to establish an allegation made by a party is on the party making the allegation. The test would be, 
who would fail if no evidence is led.”’ 


And by the Hon’ble Allahabad High Court in the case of District Administrative Committee, U.P. P.A.C.C.S.C. 
Services v. Secretary-cum-G.M. District Co-operative Bank Ltd. 2010 (126) FLR 519; wherein it has been held as 
under: 


“The submission is that even if the petitioner failed to lead the evidence, burden was on the shoulders of the 
respondent to prove the termination order as illegal. He was required to lead evidence first which he failed. 
A perusal of the impugned award also does not show that any evidence either oral or documentary was led 
by the respondent. In the case of no evidence, the reference has to be dismissed.” 


As the claimant/workman did not turn up for cross-examination, so it is a case of no evidence filed on behalf of 
workman in support of case, liable to be dismissed. 


For the foregoing reasons, the case is dismissed and; and the workman is not entitled for any relief. 
Award as above.

FACTS OF THE CASE 

On 06.04.2015, claimant filed written statement stating therein the following facts in brief as under: 


Workman/claimant was initially appointed in the month of May 1995, on post of jamadaar cum chaprasi on casual 
basis and the said capacity he started working and discharging his duties till 29.04.2006.

of the workman, is only to law because retain service of his juniors so the same is clear violation of Section 25G & 
25H of the Act. 


Workman/claimant since the date of retrenchment is without any job and at the verge of starvation. 


Accordingly it is prayed by claimant, that order of termination/retrenchment may be set aside and he may reinstated 
back in his services, from the date he was retrenched, with all services benefits should be given to him. 


On behalf of respondent written statement was filed on 06.04.2016, in which the following objections/preliminary 
objections has been taken:- 


1). The present reference is devoid of any merits and bad in the eyes of law and as such not maintainable. 
2). The reference order is itself not clear in regard alleged date of termination. 


3). No cause of dispute rather an Industrial Dispute existed on the alleged date of termination, i.e. 30.4.2006, between 
the Opposite Parties and Ravindra Prasad Gupta. 


Further it has been pleaded by the respondent in their written statement as under:- 


a). The present case has been filed after an inordinate delay of more than 7 years before the Learned Regional Labour 
Commissioner, Lucknow and reference is made by the Central Government dated 17.02.2015 i.e. after a lapse of 9 
years from the alleged date of termination. 


b). The Learned Regional Labour Commissioner, Lucknow, without proper application of mind, contrary to the 
settled principles of law acting like a postman send the report to the Central Government for referring the matter for 
adjudication. 


c). As per the provisions of section 2 A sub section (3), of the Industrial Disputes’ Act, 1947, any application for 
adjudicating any dispute or difference between a workman and his employer connected with, or arising out of

discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination shall be made to the Labour Court or Tribunal before the expiry of 
three years from the date of such discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination. 


d). A limitation of three years for raising an industrial dispute has been provided in the Industrial Disputes' Act, 1947, 
itself and provisions of any extension of limitation period has not been provided in the Industrial Disputes' Act, 1947, 
by the legislature. 


e). On the basis of the above mentioned averments, it is requested that the present reference dated 17.02.2015, should 
be rejected as bad in the eyes of law and as such not maintainable. 


On behalf of respondent evidence on affidavit of Shri Ashotosh Anand, Chief Manager, HRM of the bank filed, he 
was cross examined on 04.05.2015. 


On behalf of workman on 27.06.2016 rejoinder affidavit has been filed denying the averments as taken by respondent. 


On 05.11.2020, workman/claimant has filed evidence on affidavit (Examination in Chief) and he was cross examined 
on 07.01.2021, by respondent. 


During the pendency of case as per notification dated 26.11.2019, moved by the Ministry Of Finance (Department of 
Financial Services), relevant portion quoted herein below:- 


Baroda Uttar Pradesh Gramin Bank, Kashi Gomti Samyut Gramin Bank and Purvanchal Bank (hereinafter 
referred to as "the transferor Regional Rural Banks") sponsored by the Bank of Baroda, Union Bank of India 
and State Bank of India in the State of Uttar Pradesh are hereby amalgamated into a single Regional Rural 
Bank which shall be called as Baroda U.P. Bank (hereinafter referred to as "the transferee Regional Rural 
Bank") with its head office at Gorakhpur under the sponsorship of Bank of Baroda. 


Accordingly as per the said notification respondent 10.1 0 & 1B were imp leaded as party, In view of the law laid 
down by Hon’ble Madras High Court in case of Palanisamy R vs. Presiding Officer, Labour Court, 2001 
LawSuit(Mad) 152, and also in the case of Shri Kanchi Kamakoti Peetam Charitable Trust Hospital vs. Industrial 
Tribunal & Others, 2004 (100) FLR 1166. 


I have heard Shri Parvez Alam legal representative of claimant, and Shri Adarsh Jagdhari learned counsel for 
respondent. 


After hearing the parties/their legal representative and Advocate, the first point to be considered the point to be 
consider in the present case:- 


A). whether the reference dated 17.02.2015, is vague and on the basis of the same no cause of action arises on the 
part of workman/claimant to file present claim petition. 


In order to decide the said dispute it would be appropriate to go through Section 10 of the Industrial Dispute Act. 
10. Section 10 of Industrial Disputes Act reads thus: 


"10. Reference of disputes to Boards, Courts or Tribunals. (1) [Where the appropriate Government is of 
opinion that any industrial dispute exists or is apprehended, it may at any time), by order in writing,- 


(a) refer the dispute to a Board for promoting a settlement thereof; or 
(b) refer any matter appearing to be connected with or relevant to the dispute to a Court for inquiry; or 


[(c) refer the dispute or any matter appearing to be connected with, or relevant to, the dispute, if it relates to 
any matter specified in the Second Schedule, to a Labour Court for adjudication; or 


(d) refer the dispute or any matter appearing to be connected with, or relevant to, the dispute, whether it 
relates to any matter specified in the Second Schedule or the Third Schedule, to a Tribunal for adjudication: 


Provided that where the dispute relates to any matter specified in the Third Schedule and is not likely to 
affect more than one hundred workmen, the appropriate Government may, if it so thinks fit, make the 
reference to a Labour Court under clause (c):]" 


11. Plain reading of aforesaid provision would show that when industrial dispute exists or is apprehended, appropriate 
Government can refer dispute to Court for enquiry or if relates to any matter specified in Second Schedule to Labour 
Court for adjudication or make Reference to Tribunal, if dispute relates to matters specified in Second Schedule or 
Third Schedule. It is, therefore, obvious that Reference can be made only when industrial disputes exists or is 
apprehended by Competent Authority. 


13. The aforesaid legal position would make explicit that existence of industrial dispute is a paramount and important 
consideration while dealing with Reference. 


Only existent or apprehended industrial disputes can be referred for consideration of Court or Tribunal. However, at 
the time of taking decision whether Reference to be made or not, appropriate Government need not venture into 


4068 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 9, 2026/VAISAKHA 19, 1948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


merits of dispute, as making Reference is only administrative function. Only because Reference is made under 
Section 10(1), Court or Tribunal is not precluded from entering into aspects of delay and laches or to record findings 
as to existence or non-existence of dispute. 


In case of Prabhakar v. Joint Director, Sericulture Department and "another, 2015 (147) FLR 341 (SC), the 
Hon’ble Supreme Court considered and held the impact of delay and laches in Reference made under Section 10(1) of 
Industrial Disputes Act and observed in paragraph No. 14 as under: 


"40. An industrial dispute has to be referred by the appropriate Government for adjudication and the 
workman cannot approach the Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal directly, except in those cases which are 
covered by Section 2-A of the Act. Reference is made under Section 10 of the Act in those cases where the 
appropriate Government forms an opinion that ‘any industrial dispute exists or is apprehended’. The words 
‘industrial dispute exists' are of paramount importance unless there is an existence of an industrial dispute 
(or the dispute is apprehended or it is apprehended such a dispute may arise in near future), no reference is 
to be made. Thus, existence or apprehension of an industrial dispute is a sine qua non for making the 
reference. No doubt, at the time of taking a decision whether a reference is to be made or not, the 
appropriate Government is not to go into the merits of the dispute. Making of reference is only an 
administrative function. At the same time, on the basis of material on record, satisfaction of the existence of 
the industrial dispute or the apprehension of an industrial dispute is necessary. Such existence/apprehension 
of industrial dispute, thus, becomes a condition precedent, though it will be only subjective satisfaction 
based on material on record. Since, we are not concerned with the satisfaction dealing with cases where 
there is apprehended industrial dispute, discussion that follows would confine to existence of an industrial 
dispute. Dispute or difference arises when one party make a demand and other party rejects the same. It is 
held by this Court in number of cases that before raising the industrial dispute making of demand is a 
necessary pre-condition. In such a scenario, if the services of a workman are terminated and he does not 
make the demand and/or raise the issue alleging wrongful termination immediately thereafter or within 
reasonable time and raises the same after considerable lapse of period, whether it can be said that industrial 
dispute still exist. Since there is no period of limitation, it gives right to the workman to raise the dispute 
even belatedly. However, if the dispute is raised after a long period, it has to be seen as to whether such a 
dispute still exists? Thus, notwithstanding the fact that law of limitation does not apply, it is to be shown by 
the workman that there is a dispute in praesenti. For this purpose, he has to demonstrate that even if 
considerable period has lapsed and there are laches and delays, such delay has not resulted into making the 
industrial dispute seized to exist. Therefore, if the workman is able to give satisfactory explanation for these 
laches and delays and demonstrate that the circumstances discloses that issue is still alive, delay would not 
come in his way because of the reason that law of limitation has no application. On the other hand, if 
because of such delay dispute no longer remains alive and is to be treated as "dead", then it would be non- 
existent dispute which cannot be referred." 


Thus it can be held on the point in issue that for raising industrial dispute demand is precondition. In case, employee 
fails to make demand, dispute cannot be referred. 


From the perusal of claim statement filed by claimant on 06.05.2005, undisputed facts which emerged out that he was 
initially appointed as casual labour on the post of jamadaar cum chaprasi in the purvanchal gramin bank, Gorakhpur, 
now known as Baroda UP bank, in the branch saleempur dewaria, in the said capacity he worked and discharged his 
duties up till 29.04.2006, his services were retrenched/terminated, so workman raise a Industrial Dispute and by 
reference dated 17.02.2015, the same was referred to this Tribunal for adjudication quoted here an above. 


Further in the written statement filed by respondent, a preliminary objections/plea was taken that the reference in 
question is vague as alias date of termination as mentioned in the reference dated 30.04.2006, is incorrect and as 
matter of fact on record, thereafter workman work with the respondent/bank.

27.01.2021 he was cross examined, in which he has stated as under:-

था| 


2013 के लिए काम का पैसा मित्र गया। इस पैसे का कोर्ड विवाद नहीं है। 2006 तक जो काम किया था उसका भी पैसा 
मिना था।/2013 के बाव से अब तक बैंक में काम नहीं किया हैं। 2006 में निकानने के बाव 2013 में बैंक ने GE बुलाया

Accordingly from the cross examination of the workman, it is clearly established that he has worked as a casual 
employer in the bank in the year 2013, as such in view of the provision of Section 10(1) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(1)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 9, 2026/वैशाख 19, 1948 4069 


as quoted here an above as well the facts which is stated u/s of the Section 10(1) of the Act, no dispute was in 
existence which is paramount condition for making a reference in question not as per law. 


Further in the present case from the language of reference it is clearly established that the appropriate government has 
referred to decide the dispute that is the action on the part of respondent thereby retrenching the services of 
Shri Ravindra Prasad Gupta/claimant, on 30.06.2006, is as per law and valid, if not then what relief he is granted. 


As stated above in the present case the workman/Shri Ravindra Prasad Gupta, has himself admitted the facts that after
